st: Whisk [[2 cups]] flour, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.25 tsp]] nutmeg in a bowl. Add the eggs and [[0.75 cup]] milk and beat with a wooden spoon into a thick, sticky batter.
Rest the batter for 15 minutes while you bring a large pot of well-salted water to a gentle boil.
Melt [[1 tbsp]] butter in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onions for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until deep golden brown. Set aside.
Press the batter through a spaetzle press or the large holes of a colander into the simmering water, working in batches.
Cook each batch for 2 to 3 minutes until the dumplings float, then lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Heat the oven to 200°F (95°C). Layer the warm dumplings and the grated cheese in a baking dish, tossing with the remaining [[2 tbsp]] butter, and keep warm until the cheese melts.
Stir gently, season with pepper, and top with the fried onions before serving.
Heat a wide skillet over medium heat and add [[1.5 cups]] cornmeal. Toast it dry for 4 minutes, stirring, until it smells nutty.
Add [[2 tbsp]] butter and stir until the cornmeal is coated.
Bring [[1 cup]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt to a boil in a small pot and pour it over the cornmeal in a thin stream while stirring.
Cook, stirring and chopping with a wooden spoon, for 5 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Add [[1 cup]] hot milk, lower the heat and keep stirring and breaking up lumps for 10 minutes until you have loose crumbs.
Stir in the remaining [[1 tbsp]] butter and [[1 tbsp]] sugar and fry for 3 minutes until the crumbs are lightly golden and dry.
Serve warm in bowls with the jam on the side.
Put the ham hock, onion and [[8 cups]] water in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim the foam, then simmer covered for 1 hour.
Lift the ham hock out, let it cool slightly, then pull the meat off the bone and chop it. Keep the broth simmering.
Cook the chopped bacon in a skillet for 6 minutes until crisp. Set it aside with its fat.
Mix [[1 cup]] flour, [[1 cup]] cornmeal, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Beat in the eggs and just enough milk, about [[0.5 cup]], for a stiff dough.
With wet hands shape the dough into small dumplings about the size of a walnut.
Remove the onion from the broth. Drop the dumplings in, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until firm and cooked through.
Stir the ham meat back in and ladle into bowls with some broth, topping each with the crisp bacon and a spoon of its fat.
Put the whole unpeeled potatoes in a pot of cold salted water, bring to a boil and cook for 12 minutes. They should still be firm in the middle.
Drain the potatoes and chill them in the fridge for at least 30 minutes, then peel them.
Fry the bacon in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat for 5 minutes until crisp. Remove it with a slotted spoon and wipe out most of the fat.
Coarsely grate the cold potatoes into a bowl and toss with [[1 tsp]] salt, the pepper, the onion and the bacon.
Melt [[1.5 tbsp]] butter in the skillet over medium heat. Add the potato mixture and press into an even cake without packing it too tightly.
Cook for 12 minutes without stirring until the bottom is deep golden. Slide it onto a plate.
Melt [[1.5 tbsp]] butter in the pan, flip the rosti back in upside down and cook for 10 minutes more until both sides are crisp.
Slide onto a board, cut into wedges and serve hot.
Combine [[2 cups]] milk, [[1 cup]] water, [[2 tbsp]] sugar and a pinch of salt in a saucepan and heat until just simmering.
Slowly pour [[1 cup]] cornmeal into the liquid in a thin stream while whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Switch to a wooden spoon, lower the heat, and cook for 15 minutes, stirring often, until the porridge is thick and pulls away from the pot.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] butter and cover. Let it rest for 5 minutes.
Melt the remaining [[1 tbsp]] butter in a skillet and stir in [[1 tbsp]] sugar and the cinnamon if using.
Spoon the porridge into bowls and pour the sweet butter over the top before serving warm.
